slides.title: KINETIC ENERGY AND THE WORK-ENERGY THEOREM
THE RULES
slides.note: Net work done on an object equals its change in kinetic energy.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 1
slides.problem: A 2 kg cart moves at 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?

slides.title: EXAMPLE 2
slides.problem: A 10 N force pushes a box 4 m along the floor, in the same direction. How much work is done?

slides.title: WATCH OUT
slides.wrong: Doubling the speed doubles the KE
points: KE depends on v², so doubling speed quadruples KE.
A force perpendicular to the motion (θ = 90°) does zero work.

pageTitle: Kinetic Energy and the Work-Energy Theorem
description: KE = ½mv², the work formula, and the work-energy theorem with two worked examples.
